title: Input symbol in a canonical pairing configuration
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Boolean Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $s$ be a configuration of $M$ on $x$. For any captured word $u$, optional administrative state $q$, natural number $i\le |x|$, integer offset $j$, and output word $o$, the symbol scanned on the input tape in the corresponding canonical pairing configuration is the symbol of $x$ at index $i$, or no symbol if $i=|x|$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Boolean Turing machine
replaced:
Let $M$ be a finite machine, $x$ an input, and $i \le |x|$. In every canonical
pairing configuration over $M$ on input $x$ at input position $i$, the symbol read
by the input head is the $i$-th bit of $x$ when $i < |x|$, and the blank when
$i = |x|$.
